title: Bypassing Dead Code Warnings (Suppressions of Cruft)
pattern: Attributing dead or unused modules, functions, or structs with `#[allow(dead_code)]` or `#[allow(unused)]` instead of resolving or deleting them.
why_bad: Hides architectural decay from the compiler and automated tooling, retaining dead code that bloats compile times and confuses future readers.
detection: Occurrence of unused items decorated with `#[allow(dead_code)]` or `#[allow(unused)]` within non-library codebases.
counterexample: Public library APIs, external crates, or FFI bindings where code is consumed externally.
fix: Delete the unused code and its associated suppression attribute.
source: Sandi Metz, *Practical Object-Oriented Design* (2019), Chapter 9 ("Designing Cost-Effective Tests - Delete Unused Code"), p. 179.
